ellie: Heads-up — bringing up a HF model (x-llama-chat-aux) and hit an annoying trust_remote_code / autoloading edge case. Converter ran but tokenizer lost special tokens and the repo's chat_template field got dropped. Anyone seen this?
soham: Can you paste the exact convert command + the top of config.json? Usually the traceback helps.
ellie: Ran the usual: `python scripts/convert_hf_to_redwood.py --repo x-llama-chat-aux --trust_remote_code true`
ellie: Error snip: ```Traceback (most recent call last): File "loader.py", line 213, in load_model cls = auto_map["AutoModel"] KeyError: 'AutoModel' During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: AttributeError: 'CustomConfig' object has no attribute 'hidden_size'```
matt: ugh, yeah. Some HF repos register their custom classes under different auto_map keys or only export them when trust_remote_code=True. Our converter expects a standard auto_map entry. If the model uses a custom config class that doesn't subclass the usual, fields like special_tokens_map can be omitted.
soham: Two quick workarounds: 1) locally `from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoTokenizer` with trust_remote_code=True, load+re-save to a clean folder so HF canonicalizes things; 2) patch config.json to include explicit `auto_map` entries.
ellie: Tried trust_remote_code=True but the converter step that normalizes config strips unknown fields — I think the converter's validation removes `chat_template` and custom keys. Here's the top of the repo config.json we got: ```{ "architectures": ["CustomForCausalLM"], "auto_map": {"CustomConfig": "custom_package.CustomConfig"}, "chat_template": {"system": "You are helpful"}, "special_tokens_map": null }```
matt: if special_tokens_map is null that's a red flag. You can add `"tokenizer_class": "custom_package.CustomTokenizer"` and include a `special_tokens_map.json` next to tokenizer files. Or in config.json: `"auto_map": {"AutoConfig": "custom_package.CustomConfig", "AutoModel": "custom_package.CustomForCausalLM"}` — that tends to make the loader happy.
infra-bot: deploy-checker: conversion failed on step `validate_tokenizer` — falling back to cpu-runner for manual verification.
soham: If you want to avoid trusting remote code on Redwood host, do the local load/resave: ```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoConfig
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('x-llama-chat-aux', trust_remote_code=True)
conf = AutoConfig.from_pretrained('x-llama-chat-aux', trust_remote_code=True)
# ensure special tokens
if not tok.special_tokens_map:
    tok.add_special_tokens({'eos_token': '</s>', 'bos_token': '<s>'})
# save a normalized copy
tok.save_pretrained('./x-llama-chat-aux-normalized')
conf.save_pretrained('./x-llama-chat-aux-normalized')
```
ellie: Nice — i'll try that and then re-run the converter pointing at the normalized folder. If that still strips `chat_template` i'll push a small change to the converter to whitelist chat_template.
matt: also drop a `special_tokens_map.json` with the tokenizer export; some of these custom tokenizers serialize differently and our validate step misses them.
ellie: Will do. Thanks — will report back. :thumbsup:
soham: +1 — ping me if you want me to run the local resave.
ellie: pinged — trying now, will update in this thread. :eyes:
